correctness.rationale: For all integers q,d at least two, the distance-jump radial birth/death rates are 2(d-j)(q-1) and 2j, while the full marked success intensity is 2d(q-1)-2 times the adjacency indicator. Differentiation of the full marked generator gives variance rate as mean plus twice the reversible Poisson Green form. Summing the radial Poisson equation across each cut yields the exact binomial-tail expression. Every summand is positive. Uniform fixed-q tail bounds prove the 2/[d(q-1)q^d] leading excess with coefficient one after normalization. Nine independently constructed full-state generator comparisons succeeded; they corroborate rather than prove all dimensions.

value.rationale: Total successful-jump counting noise is a physically motivated transport/activity observable. A complete exact q,d classification separates Poissonian one-factor geometry from strictly super-Poissonian multifactor exclusion and quantifies the surprisingly exponentially small rare-blocking effect with a sharp fixed-alphabet coefficient. This is more informative than stationary mean activity or a generic pseudoinverse formula. Limitations: only two particles, homogeneous rates, global success counts and fixed q for asymptotics.
